topic.title: Airbnb Was Saved by $40 Boxes of Cereal

title: Airbnb Sold Cereal for $40 a Box
description:
Why did Airbnb's founders sell breakfast cereal for $40 a box?
In 2008 investors turned the home-sharing start-up down, so its founders made election cereal, and it got them into Y Combinator.
Sources: CNBC (Apr 2023).
Based on public records and reporting. Not financial or legal advice.

lines.text: Airbnb's founders once sold cereal at $40 a box, to stay afloat.
And not just any cereal: the boxes were Obama O's and Cap'n McCain's, made for that year's US election. So why was a website for spare rooms selling breakfast?
Airbnb rented air mattresses in strangers' homes. Brian Chesky ran it with two co-founders in San Francisco.
The investors they wrote to turned them down, or never wrote back.
So the founders made the cereal themselves. Would anyone pay that much? They sold more than 1,000 boxes.
Then the cereal won over Y Combinator, the start-up school. It put in $20,000 for 6% of Airbnb.
All told, the cereal brought in $30,000: more money than Y Combinator's whole first cheque.
Cereal or air mattresses: which one would you have funded? Every Airbnb you book today goes back to the day
